newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close sharply higher.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished higher on Tuesday in the last 1996 trading day on rising money demand before the three-day New Year's holiday, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 5.465 percent against Monday's 5.219 close, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.75 against 5.00-5.10.
Tuesday was also the last trading day for the monthly reserve period, which normally would end on January 3 in the absence of a holiday.
Dealers expected the money rates to remain at high levels when the market reopens on Saturday.
The bond market reported no trade in the afternoon. Government bond yields rose slightly earlier on expected oil price hikes.
Economics ministry said on Tuesday it had authorised Chinese petrol prices by nine percent starting Janaury 1 to alleviate growing budgetary shortfalls.

Wednesday and Thursday are national holidays. All markets and banks will close on Friday for banks' accounting settlement, although government offices and private business will open as usual. Trading resumes on Saturday. -- Rachel Lee (5080815)
